Concise Clinical Note

Consult Summary:
23-year-old woman with 3–4 day history of constant, worsening midline lower-abdominal pain (8/10) with light post-menstrual vaginal bleeding and mild nausea; ectopic pregnancy must be ruled out. Arranged urgent face-to-face abdominal/pelvic assessment and repeat pregnancy test today.

History:
• Presenting complaint: Constant lower-abdominal (“tummy”) pain, midline below umbilicus.  
• Onset/duration: Began “a few days ago,” progressively worse.  
• Severity: 8/10.  
• Associated symptoms: Light pink vaginal bleeding since after normal period 2 weeks ago; small amount vaginal discharge; occasional nausea (no vomiting); constipation last week now resolved.  
• Pertinent negatives: No fever, chills, dyspnea, shoulder pain, syncope, dysuria, hematuria, hematochezia, weight loss.  
• Past medical history: None reported. No prior surgeries or pregnancies.  
• Allergies: Amoxicillin – allergic reaction unspecified.  
• Medications/contraception: Etonogestrel implant (Implanon) inserted ~1 year ago; no other regular meds.  
• Social / preventive: 23-year-old school teacher; lives with husband and his family; sexually active; non-smoker; does not drink alcohol; no recreational drugs; travel abroad >1 year ago.

Examination:
No physical examination or vital signs obtained (video visit only).

Impression:
Acute pelvic/lower-abdominal pain – gynae etiology must be excluded.  
1. Ectopic pregnancy – high priority to rule out given pelvic pain + light bleeding; last pregnancy test 1 month ago; implant failure rare but possible.  
2. Pelvic inflammatory disease – possible given pain, light bleeding, discharge; no fever but exam pending.  
3. Ovarian torsion or hemorrhagic/ruptured cyst – constant severe pain, reproductive age; localization not clearly unilateral.

Plan:
• Urgent in-person appointment arranged via support line for abdominal and pelvic examination.  
• Patient to perform a urine pregnancy test today; instructed to call back immediately if positive.  
• Advise emergency attendance if pain worsens, develops shoulder-tip pain, dizziness, vomiting preventing oral intake, or heavy bleeding.  
• No medications prescribed during tele-visit.  
• Documentation of allergy noted.  
• Await in-person exam; consider pelvic ultrasound, serum β-hCG, STI screen, CBC if ectopic ruled out.

Quality checks
● Missing elements: vitals, abdominal/pelvic exam findings, detailed allergy reaction, complete medication list, bowel/urinary diary, formal follow-up date.  
● Conflicts: None material between transcript and DDx.  
● Transcript quality: Patient identifiers redacted; some audio gaps and unclear answers; overall history adequate but physical exam absent.
